newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: One dies after Christian-Moslem clash in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: One dies after Christian-Moslem clash in Pakistan.

text.p: One man died after Christians and Moslems clashed in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Thursday and at least 17 people, including a policeman, were wounded, local officals said.
Police and hospital sources said a Moslem, apparently hit by police fire, died in hospital, prompting authorities to impose a curfew in a troubled suburb of Khanewal town, southern Punjab.

Witnesses said army trucks and police cars patrolled the streets in the mainly Christian Shantinagar suburb after the incident, in which Moslems accused the Christians of desecrating the Koran. The Christians denied the allegation.

The trouble began on Wednesday night when pages torn from Koran, carrying the names of several Christians living in Shantinagar, were thrown into a mosque in the Railway Colony district where Moslems were praying, the witnesses said.

Moslems, accusing the Christians of desecration, set fire to a church in Shantinagar. When Christians learned of the incident on Thursday morning, they came to Shantinagar from nearby villages and battled Moslems who had also flocked to the scene.
Most of Pakistan's 131 million people are Moslems, but there is a small Christian minority.
